name: YEMEN
tagline: Land of the Queen of Sheba
lead: Yemen sits at the tip of Arabia, beside the sea. Its highlands had great kingdoms before most European cities existed. The legendary Queen of Sheba ruled here 3,000 years ago. Today it has mud-brick skyscrapers.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: One of the world's oldest cities

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Yemen's highlands are the wettest part of Arabia. Monsoon rains feed terraced farms 2,000 m up. Two seas squeeze Yemen into a horn shape.
The Empty Quarter, the biggest sand desert on Earth, lies to the east. Far offshore, the Socotra islands sit closer to Somalia than to Sana'a.
animals: The Arabian leopard is Yemen's national animal. Fewer than 200 survive on remote highland cliffs. Nubian ibex and Arabian wolves also climb the rocky hills.
On Socotra, nearly 700 species live nowhere else. The dragon blood tree looks like a giant umbrella. It bleeds bright red sap when cut.
culture: Yemenis have built with mud for thousands of years. Shibam's tower blocks rise up to 11 storeys. People call it the 'Manhattan of the Desert'.
In the 15th century, Sufi monks in Yemen first brewed coffee. It kept them awake for night prayers. The port of Mocha gave mocha coffee its name.
history: Three thousand years ago, the Kingdom of Saba controlled the incense road from India to the Mediterranean. Frankincense and myrrh were worth more than gold.
Mocha ran the world's coffee trade until the 1600s. Then Dutch traders smuggled coffee seedlings to their colonies and broke Yemen's hold.
wows: Shibam's mud towers are the world's oldest high-rise apartments.
Dragon blood tree resin has been paint and medicine for over 2,000 years.
Jabal An-Nabi Shu'ayb, at 3,666 m, is Arabia's highest peak.
The Marib Dam, built around the 8th century BC, watered huge farms.
About 37% of Socotra's plants grow nowhere else on Earth.
The word 'mocha' comes from Al-Mukha, a Yemeni port.
People have lived in Old Sana'a for over 2,500 years.

myths.fact: Socotra belongs to Yemen. UNESCO named it a World Heritage Site in 2008.

myths.myth: Coffee beans grow on bean plants
myths.fact: They are seeds inside a red fruit called a coffee cherry.
